source_name: MONSTAT — Statistički godišnjak / Statistical Yearbook
why_relevant: Single consolidated annual PDF carrying long back-series across every domain (population, trade, tourism, national accounts, ICT, finance). Ideal for one-shot historical backfill of denominators instead of scraping dozens of individual release series, and bilingual sr/en in one file.

source_name: MONSTAT — Mjesečni statistički pregled (Monthly Statistical Review / Bilten)
why_relevant: Monthly cross-domain bulletin published since 2008 and reported by MONSTAT's own user survey as its most-used data source. Gives one predictable monthly artefact bundling retail turnover, prices, tourism and labour indicators — a low-cost high-frequency monitoring anchor for the whole cell.

source_name: MONSTAT — Kalendar objavljivanja / Statistical Release Calendar
why_relevant: Legally required advance publication calendar. Turns the whole MONSTAT estate from blind polling into scheduled collection: tells the collector exactly when retail turnover, tourism, ICT and national accounts releases land, and flags methodology changes and postponements.

source_name: MONSTAT — Metapodaci / metodološka dokumentacija (metadata & methodology explorer)
why_relevant: Per-survey metadata pages (legal basis, sample, periodicity, definitions, data sources). Critical for knowing whether an indicator is comparable across years and which administrative body actually supplies the underlying data — several metadata entries name external suppliers (e.g. customs revenue overview supplied by the customs administration), which is a snowball vector to fiscal sources.

source_name: MONSTAT — Popis stanovništva 2023 / Census and demography (population and household counts)
why_relevant: The 2023 census and the demographic estimates series give the population and household base for every per-capita payment metric (cards per capita, ATMs per 100k inhabitants, POS per 1000 inhabitants) and — via municipality-level counts — for coastal-versus-inland acceptance density analysis.

source_name: MONSTAT — Cijene / Prices (CPI, HICP) and Registri (statistical business register)
source_subtype: price indices + statistical business register publications
why_relevant: Two supporting series in one cell area: CPI/HICP to deflate nominal card and retail values into real terms, and the statistical business register (broj privrednih subjekata by activity and municipality) which is the merchant-population denominator for POS penetration ('POS terminals per active retail enterprise').

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (Ministry of Finance) — institutional site and document library
why_relevant: Publisher of monthly budget execution reports, quarterly/annual central and general government debt reports, the budget law and the Economic Reform Programme (PER) with its macroeconomic and fiscal framework chapters. Provides the fiscal backdrop and forward macro projections against which payments-market growth is judged; reported Q1 2026 gross public debt of EUR 5,133.5m (59.9% of GDP).

source_name: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore (Revenue and Customs Administration) — fiscalization authority
source_subtype: tax and customs administration / fiscalization operator
why_relevant: Operator of Montenegro's mandatory electronic fiscalization system (in force since 1 June 2021), in which EVERY invoice — cash AND cashless — is reported to the tax authority in real time and receives a unique fiscal identifier. This is the only national dataset that structurally distinguishes cash from cashless transactions at invoice level across the whole retail economy; even aggregate disclosures from it would be the highest-value cash-usage evidence outside CBCG. Also publishes customs revenue collection overviews that MONSTAT itself reuses.

source_name: elektronskafiskalizacija.me — official e-fiscalization information portal (SEP/EFI)
why_relevant: Authoritative documentation layer for the fiscalization scheme: technical specifications, payment-method (način plaćanja) code lists used on every fiscal invoice, business-premises (poslovni prostor) and cash-register/ENU registration rules. The payment-method taxonomy is directly relevant to how card, cash and account-transfer transactions are officially classified in Montenegro, and the registration rules define what counts as a POS-equipped premises.

source_name: Data.gov.me — Portal otvorenih podataka Crne Gore (national open data portal)
why_relevant: Legally established central open-data portal where public bodies — including the Ministry of Finance and statistical/fiscal administrations — publish machine-readable datasets. CKAN-based, so it exposes organisation and tag filters and, typically, a REST API, making it the cheapest structured-ingest route into Montenegrin public-sector data and a discovery index of which body publishes what.

source_name: Eurostat — enlargement countries statistics (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Independent aggregator that re-publishes MONSTAT's transmitted data (including the ICT household survey, national accounts and trade) in harmonised, EU-comparable form with a documented API/bulk-download layer. Solves two problems at once: cross-country benchmarking of Montenegro's card/e-commerce penetration against peers, and a cleaner machine-readable channel than scraping MONSTAT PDFs.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — dataset on IMF Data portal
why_relevant: Core supranational supply-side database for ATM and POS terminal counts, per 100,000 adults and per 1,000 km2, plus branches, deposit/loan accounts and (recent vintages) mobile-money and digital-payment series. Montenegro is a reporting jurisdiction; 2025 release covers 163 economies, 121 series, 2004-2024. This is the single best cross-country-comparable ATM/POS density series for ME.

source_name: IMF FAS annual results press release / Highlights report
why_relevant: Announces each annual FAS vintage, its coverage changes and new series (POS pilot disaggregated rural/urban, fintech lending, gender splits). Best trigger signal for a refresh of the Montenegro FAS pull and for knowing which new indicators became available.

source_name: IMF Montenegro country page (Article IV, country reports, mission statements)
why_relevant: Hub for all IMF output on Montenegro: Article IV staff reports with banking-sector and payments annexes, selected issues papers, technical assistance reports, and the statistical appendix tables. Snowballs into individual country reports (e.g. CR 25/304, 2025 Article IV concluded November 2025).

source_name: IMF Country Report No. 25/304 — Montenegro 2025 Article IV Consultation
why_relevant: Most recent full staff report; contains banking-sector soundness tables, credit and deposit aggregates, and macro-financial context (growth 3.2% 2024/H1-2025, inflation 4.9% Sept 2025) plus EU-accession-2028 framing that drives payments-modernisation policy.

source_name: IMF Financial Soundness Indicators (FSI / FSIC dataset)
why_relevant: Standardised banking-sector soundness series (capital adequacy, NPLs, liquidity, profitability) reported by the Central Bank of Montenegro to the IMF; gives cross-country-comparable context for the banking market that underpins card/POS acquiring economics. Montenegro received IMF TA specifically on FSI compilation (2019 TA report).

source_name: IMF Data portal (data.imf.org) — general dataset catalogue (IFS, MFS, BOP)
why_relevant: Umbrella catalogue for all IMF statistical datasets in which Montenegro appears (International Financial Statistics, Monetary and Financial Statistics, Balance of Payments incl. remittance/travel credits). Portal was re-platformed, so old ?sk= query-string links coexist with new /en/datasets/ paths — worth mapping once.

source_name: World Bank Microdata Library — Global Findex collection (respondent-level microdata)
why_relevant: Respondent-level Findex files allow custom Montenegro cuts (age, income quintile, urban/rural, gender) that the headline indicators do not publish — e.g. card-payment use among older or rural adults, a key segmentation input for POS/ATM strategy.

source_name: World Bank Data360 — hosted IMF FAS and partner datasets
why_relevant: New World Bank cross-agency data platform that re-hosts IMF FAS and many other partner datasets with a unified API; often easier to query than the IMF portal and useful as a redundancy path when data.imf.org changes URL structure.

source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
why_relevant: Central-bank questionnaire covering payment-system infrastructure, retail instruments, oversight, interoperability and national payment strategies for 100+ jurisdictions (6th round released Oct 2023). If Montenegro's CBCG responded, this is one of the few standardised international views of ME payment-system architecture.

source_name: Remittance Prices Worldwide (World Bank)
why_relevant: Corridor-level cost of sending money, covering 377 corridors from 48 sending to 111 receiving countries. Relevant to Montenegro as a remittance-receiving economy (remittance inflows ~12.6% of GDP in 2020 per WB-derived series) and to cash-out/ATM demand. Montenegro's presence as a receiving corridor must be verified in the DataBank tables.

source_name: KNOMAD / World Bank Migration and Development Briefs and remittance inflow matrices
why_relevant: Annual/semi-annual remittance inflow and outflow estimates by country plus bilateral remittance matrices; standard supranational source for Montenegro remittance volumes. Note KNOMAD's hosting arrangement ran 2013-2024, so continuity of the series under a new home should be checked.

source_name: Eurostat — Enlargement / candidate-country statistics hub
why_relevant: Entry point to Eurostat's collection of Montenegrin data supplied by MONSTAT under IPA statistical alignment, and to the 'Enlargement countries - statistical overview' and factsheet series. Snowballs into specific Eurostat databrowser codes where ME appears as a non-EU reporting country.
